user: Design a bench rack for 40 2.0 mL microcentrifuge tubes. It is a solid rectangular block 144 mm long (X), 94 mm wide (Y) and 30 mm tall (Z). It has 40 vertical holes in 5 rows (along Y) of 8 (along X), 17 mm centre-to-centre in both directions, with the hole grid centred on the block. Each hole is 11.0 mm in diameter and 26 mm deep, open at the top and closed at the bottom, leaving a 4 mm solid floor.

Design a 6-place holder for 20 mL scintillation vials, printed upright. It is a solid block 220 mm long (X), 40 mm wide (Y) and 30 mm tall (Z). Cut a single row of 6 vertical blind holes along X, 36 mm apart centre-to-centre and centred on the block in X and Y. Each hole is 28.0 mm in diameter and 26 mm deep, open at the top and leaving a 4 mm floor.

Design an adapter sleeve that lets a narrow tube sit in a wider rack hole. Print it upside down: a collar 13.0 mm in diameter and 1.5 mm thick lies on the bed (z = 0 to 1.5), and the sleeve body, 11.0 mm in outer diameter, rises from the collar to z = 18.0. A straight 6.6 mm diameter bore runs through the full height, open at both ends.

Design an L-shaped mounting bracket, printed with the base plate flat on the bed. Base plate: x from -25 to 25, y from 0 to 50, z from 0 to 5, with two 5.5 mm vertical through-holes at (x = -17, y = 38) and (x = 17, y = 38). Vertical plate: x from -25 to 25, y from 0 to 5, z from 0 to 45, standing on the back edge of the base (y = 0). Through the vertical plate (along Y) cut two 5.5 mm holes at (x = -17, z = 30) and (x = 17, z = 30).

Design a small lab funnel, printed upright with the wide opening at the top. A straight spout (tube) with 10.0 mm outer diameter runs from z = 0 to z = 25. On top of it, a cone widens from 10.0 mm outer diameter at z = 25 to 60 mm outer diameter at the rim at z = 55. The wall is 1.2 mm thick everywhere (so the spout bore is 7.6 mm), and the funnel is open at the top and at the bottom so liquid runs straight through.

Design a snap-on C-clip that grips a 8.0 mm lab-stand rod, printed flat as a 8 mm tall extrusion (Z) of a 2-D profile in the XY plane. The profile is a ring with 8.0 mm inner diameter and 3.5 mm wall (so 15.0 mm outer diameter), centred on the origin, with a 5.6 mm wide opening cut out of its -X side (everything with x < 0 and -2.8 < y < 2.8 is removed) so it snaps onto the rod.

Design a push-on cap for a tube with 12.0 mm outer diameter, printed open-end up. It is a cylinder 16.0 mm in outer diameter and 12 mm tall standing on the bed, with a 12.8 mm diameter blind bore going down from the top to leave a 3.0 mm thick closed cap at the bottom (so the skirt wall is 1.6 mm and the cap slips over the tube with 0.4 mm clearance). Around the outside, cut 10 evenly spaced vertical grip grooves over the full height, each a 2 mm diameter half-cylinder centred on the outer surface.

Design a weighted base that holds a vertical support rod, printed upright. It is a solid disc 70 mm in diameter and 5 mm thick lying on the bed (z = 0 to 5), with a central cylindrical boss 24 mm in diameter rising from the disc to z = 30, centred on the origin. A 12.0 mm diameter blind bore for the rod runs down the axis from the top of the boss to z = 5. Through the boss, cut one radial 4.5 mm set-screw hole at z = 24, from the +X side to the bore.

Design a 8-well comb for casting agarose gels, printed lying flat as a 2.0 mm thick plate (Z) on the bed. Seen from above it has a straight spine (back bar) 62 mm long (X) and 10 mm wide (Y), and 8 rectangular teeth hanging from one long edge of the spine in the -Y direction. Each tooth is 5.0 mm wide (X) and 12 mm long (Y), the gaps between neighbouring teeth are 2.0 mm, and the row of teeth is centred on the spine in X.

Design a flat drilling/marking jig: a rectangular plate 50 mm long (X), 40 mm wide (Y) and 5 mm thick lying on the bed. It has a 4 x 3 grid of 4.0 mm diameter through-holes (12 in all) at 10 mm centre-to-centre spacing in both directions, centred on the plate. Cut a rectangular orientation notch into the +Y edge, centred on the Y axis: 10 mm wide (X) and 4 mm deep (Y, measured in from the edge).

Design a two-part enclosure for a small electronics board, with both parts in the same file side by side on the bed with a 10 mm gap, so they print together. Part 1, the box: outer size 80 x 60 x 35 mm (X x Y x Z), 1.6 mm walls, 1.6 mm floor, open top. Part 2, the lid, printed upside down: a plate 80 x 60 x 2.5 mm lying on the bed, with a rectangular lip on top of it - a 1.2 mm thick wall 4 mm tall whose outer size is 76.4 x 56.4 mm, centred on the plate, so it slides into the box opening with 0.2 mm clearance per side. Place the lid on the +X side of the box.

Design a replacement control knob for a 6.0 mm D-shaft, printed with the hotplate-facing side down on the bed. The knob is a cylinder 25 mm in diameter and 15 mm tall. From the bottom face, a D-shaped blind bore goes 11 mm up into the knob: a 6.2 mm diameter circle with one side cut flat, so the distance from the flat to the opposite side of the circle is 4.9 mm. Around the outside, cut 20 evenly spaced vertical grip grooves along the full height, each a 2 mm diameter half-cylinder centred on the outer surface.
